title: Schema revision and composed chart model

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 15, audited at commit 9ae4125 (HEAD of the main checkout, tree
00fec772...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. Four files,
197 insertions.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. One blocking fix -- as committed this cannot ship, because
CI goes red before the migrations run. Plus one decision I am not going to make for
you, and two missing reference documents.

REQUIRED FIX -- the column drop breaks Sprint 4's RLS suite, and R1's own grep scope
is what let it through.

R1's criterion says: "QA1 confirms by grep across `app/` and `lib/` rather than
accepting it from this file." I ran exactly that grep against 9ae4125. It comes back
clean -- the only hits on the five column names in app/ and lib/ are the word
"longitude" inside ephemeris comments and the identifier eclipticLongitude. No
reference to any dropped column. So the criterion as written passes.

Then I ran the same grep one directory over, and supabase/tests/rls.test.ts still has:

  line 18-21  validReading() supplies place_name, latitude, longitude, timezone
  line 83     .update({ place_name: "tampered" })
  line 88     expect(data?.[0].place_name).toBe("Reykjavik, Iceland")

After 20260822224615 drops those columns, every insert built from validReading() is
rejected by PostgREST -- it errors on an unknown column rather than ignoring it -- so
beforeAll throws "setup insert failed" and takes all six tests under it with it. The
"can insert a reading" test fails on its own account, the "cannot update" test's
expect(error).toBeNull() fails because updating a nonexistent column errors, and line
88 asserts on a column that no longer exists.

Chain: rls-tests fails -> migrate is skipped (needs [build, rls-tests]) -> supabase db
push never runs -> the deploy hook never fires -> nothing reaches production. Sprint
4's gate and Sprint 5's ordering both work exactly as designed; what they are catching
is this.

Fix: remove the four place columns from validReading(), and repoint the update test at
a column that still exists -- event_date is the obvious one, still NOT NULL, still
there. Change line 83 to .update({ event_date: "1900-01-01" }) and line 88 to assert
event_date is still "1999-08-11".

This is the second time this exact shape has occurred -- Sprint 10 added positions NOT
NULL and broke the same file, for the same reason, and it was caught here rather than
in CI. So the more useful fix is to R1's criterion itself: it names the two
directories where the application lives and omits the one where the tests that gate
the deploy live. Sprint 17 does more schema work. Widen the criterion to app/, lib/
AND supabase/tests/ before then, or this recurs a third time. I could not run the RLS
suite to demonstrate the break -- no Docker here, as since Sprint 4 -- but a NOT NULL
insert of a nonexistent column is not a judgement call.

DECISION REQUIRED, not a fix I will specify -- composeChart's `applying` is
structurally always false.

composeChart calls computeAspects(positions, positions). Passing one snapshot twice
means orbLater is computed from the same data as orbNow, so `orbLater < orbNow` can
never hold and every aspect in the model comes back applying: false. Dev Team
documented this thoroughly -- in model.ts's comment, in the test file's comment, and
in a dedicated test asserting the degenerate behaviour -- so nothing is hidden and I
want that credited. R4 forbids computePositions inside composeChart, R3 fixes the
signature at (date, positions), and there is genuinely no second snapshot available.
Given those constraints the implementation is the honest option.

The problem is the shape that ships. docs/design/CHART_MODEL.md's own fixture table --
the document R7 names as the reference -- records an Application column reading
applying for 8 of its 15 rows and separating for 7. composeChart reproduces 7 of those
by coincidence and gets 8 wrong. The test correctly refuses to assert that column and
says why, which is the right call for a test and does not fix the model.

So ChartModel carries a boolean that is always false, three sprints read this model,
and model.ts's own comment says Sprint 17's prompt template plans to consume it. A
field that is structurally false is worse than an absent one, because a downstream
reader takes false to mean "separating" rather than "unknown". Options, in rough order
of how much I like them:
  - type it away: aspects: Omit<Aspect, "applying">[], or a ComposedAspect type. The
    impossibility becomes a compile error in Sprint 17 rather than a comment nobody
    re-reads.
  - make it tri-state (applying: boolean | null) so "unknown" is representable.
  - keep it, and record in CHART_MODEL.md that the Application column is not
    reproducible by composeChart, so the reference document stops disagreeing with the
    thing it is the reference for.
I am not choosing, because R3 pins the shape to PRD v2 §2.3 and I cannot read it --
see missing document 2. Whoever owns that spec should decide, and this sprint is the
cheap moment: it is the sprint that defines the shape.

MISSING DOCUMENT 1 -- docs/design/CHART_MODEL.md is untracked.
git ls-tree at 9ae4125 shows docs/design/ containing only the three Sprint 13 handoff
files. CHART_MODEL.md exists in the working tree and nowhere else. The sprint file
cites it three times, including in R7's acceptance criterion ("the fixture test
asserts specific values from CHART_MODEL.md"), and Sprints 16-18 are told to build
against this model. As committed, the reference for the criterion I just audited does
not ship, and the next reader has a test full of magic numbers with a comment pointing
at a file they do not have. I flagged it as untracked in Sprint 14's audit too. Commit
it.

MISSING DOCUMENT 2 -- PRD v2 is not in the repository.
R3 says composeChart's exports are "per PRD §2.3" and the Context names
retroactivehoroscopeprdv2poc.md. A find across the repo returns only docs/PRD_v1.md.
So R3's reference does not exist here and I cannot verify the model against it -- I can
confirm the four exports are present and coherent, which is not the same as confirming
they match the spec. Three sprints depend on this shape. If the PRD is the authority,
it belongs in docs/ next to PRD_v1.md.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET as scoped, NOT MET in substance -- see the required fix. The migration itself is
  correct and its comment reasons correctly about why the contract half is safe now.
R2 MET. All four new columns nullable, no default, nothing backfilled. An insert from
  the currently deployed version (id, event_date, positions) still succeeds.
R1/R2 ledger MET. Both migrations are timestamped, live only under
  supabase/migrations/, and each ends with its own schema_migrations insert matching
  its filename. No DDL anywhere in app/, lib/ or supabase/tests/.
R3 UNVERIFIABLE against its stated reference -- see missing document 2. ChartModel,
  ReadingModel, DateEvent and composeChart(date, positions) are all exported and
  internally coherent.
R4 MET. No computePositions call in lib/chart -- the only two mentions are comments
  explaining why it is absent. The test asserts chart.positions toBe the same
  reference rather than a clone, which is a sharper check than deep equality: it
  proves the array was passed through, not rebuilt.
R5 MET. calculationInstantForDate validates the format and round-trips the calendar
  date, then assertDateInSupportedRange enforces 1700-2100 with adapter.ts's own
  message. Both bounds tested.
R6 MET. lib/chart imports only from ../ephemeris/*. No node: import, no server-only
  anywhere in the reachable graph.
R7 MET in substance. The fixture test asserts bodyA, bodyB, aspect, orb and tightness
  for all fifteen rows plus Julian Day, elements, modalities and moon phase against
  specific recorded values -- not merely that an object came back. The one column it
  does not assert is disclosed with its reason. Note the fixture positions are stated
  to come from the engine directly rather than from composeChart, which is what keeps
  this from being circular.
R8 MET. No UI change, no events fetching, no OpenAI. The four columns ship empty.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 117 tests across 12 files, 7 new.
- The RLS suite is NOT run here and cannot be -- no Docker. That is precisely why the
  break above is invisible locally and would surface first in CI.

Notes:
1. GroundTruth's second criterion is the right one and deserves emphasis: five columns
   are being dropped from a table holding real rows including the Sprint 14 fixture.
   The static case that the fixture survives is good -- /reading/[id] reads only
   event_date and positions, neither dropped -- but "should survive" is doing real
   work in that sentence and the comparison must be value by value against Sprint 14's
   recorded table, not by eye.
2. saveReading's discarded Supabase error is explicitly deferred to Sprint 18 by this
   sprint's Out of Scope. Correct, and now tracked in a sprint file rather than only
   in my notes, which is where it should have been three sprints ago.

Re-audit after the rls.test.ts fix and a decision on `applying`. The fixture change is
a few lines in one file; keep the re-audit proportionate to that plus whatever the
decision moves.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 15, round 2. Audited at commit e3f56e7, HEAD of the main checkout,
recorded tree d43b8314... Sprint file re-read fresh. Scope: three files -- the RLS
suite repair plus the two reference documents that were missing.

VERDICT: PASS.

REQUIRED FIX -- the RLS suite. FIXED, exactly. The four dropped place columns are out
of validReading(), and the "cannot update" test is repointed at event_date, which
still exists and is still NOT NULL, with its assertion following it (updates to
"2000-01-01", asserts the row still reads "1999-08-11"). That keeps the test testing
what it was written to test -- that an anon UPDATE affects zero rows -- rather than
quietly becoming a test of a column that no longer exists.

I then re-ran the grep across everything rather than just the two directories R1
names. The only surviving references to the dropped columns anywhere are inside
supabase/migrations/, which is correct and required: those files are append-only
history and must keep describing what they did. No live code, no test, no config.

MISSING DOCUMENT 1 -- CHART_MODEL.md. FIXED, committed, 150 lines.
MISSING DOCUMENT 2 -- PRD v2. FIXED, committed as docs/PRD_v2_poc.md, 299 lines.

That second one matters more than a bookkeeping fix, because it converts R3 from
unverifiable to verified. §2.3 specifies the model shape in TypeScript, and
lib/chart/model.ts matches it field for field: ChartModel with date, julianDay,
positions, aspects (sorted tightest first), elements, modalities, moonPhase;
composeChart(date: string, positions: PlanetPosition[]): ChartModel; DateEvent with
year, text, optional sourceUrl; ReadingModel with id, chart, events, horoscope. §2.4
independently confirms the 1700-2100 bounds R5 requires and the implementation
enforces. Last round I could confirm the exports were coherent but not that they were
right. Now I can.

THE `applying` DECISION -- made, and made in the only place it could be.

The PRD being readable settles why: §2.3 pins aspects to `Aspect[]`, which carries
`applying`. So the two options I preferred -- typing the field away, or making it
tri-state -- both require amending the PRD, and neither was mine to impose. The
contradiction is upstream of this sprint: the PRD specifies a type carrying a field
and a function signature that cannot determine it.

The third option was taken. CHART_MODEL.md now carries an explicit block directly
under the aspect table stating that the Application column is not reproducible by
composeChart, why (one snapshot, and deriving a second would mean calling
computePositions, which R4 forbids so composed charts can never disagree with the row
they came from), and what it costs -- "right for 7 of these 15 rows, wrong for the
other 8", which matches my own count exactly. It closes by warning whoever wires up
Sprint 17's prompt template that they need a real second snapshot and should not read
the field as meaningful before then.

That is the right resolution given the constraint. The limitation is now recorded in
three places a downstream reader could plausibly land -- model.ts's comment, the test
file, and the reference document the sprint file points Sprints 16-18 at -- and the
reference document no longer silently disagrees with the model it describes. I would
still rather this were a compile error than a paragraph, and I said so; that is a PRD
amendment, not a Sprint 15 fix, and it is on the record for whoever owns §2.3.

Requirements coverage: R1 through R8 all met.
R1 MET, now in substance as well as by R1's stated grep scope.
R2 MET. Four nullable columns, no defaults, nothing backfilled.
R3 MET, verified against PRD §2.3 rather than inferred.
R4 MET. No computePositions in lib/chart. The test asserts chart.positions toBe the
  same array reference, which proves pass-through rather than reconstruction.
R5 MET, and now cross-checked against PRD §2.4.
R6 MET. lib/chart imports only ../ephemeris/*; no node:, no server-only.
R7 MET, and its reference document now ships with it.
R8 MET. No UI change, no events fetching, no OpenAI.

Verified by execution at e3f56e7:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 117 tests across 12 files.
- next build exits 0; route table unchanged.
- Rebuilt with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="QA1PROBESERVICEROLE" and grepped all of
  .next: absent from the entire build output.
- The RLS suite still cannot run here -- no Docker. The repair above is a reading of
  what PostgREST does with an unknown column, and CI is where it gets demonstrated.
  Same standing limitation as every sprint since Sprint 4.

Notes, not conditions:
1. R1's criterion still names only app/ and lib/. The fix landed but the criterion
   that missed it did not change, and Sprint 17 does more schema work -- its
   SECURITY DEFINER write function. This is the second time a schema change has broken
   supabase/tests/rls.test.ts (Sprint 10 was the first). Widening the standing grep
   scope to include supabase/tests/ costs nothing and is the difference between
   catching this at the gate and catching it in CI. Master Controller's call, and
   worth making before Sprint 17 is written rather than after.
2. CHART_MODEL.md line 60 still reads `applying: boolean; // false = separating` in
   the section describing lib/ephemeris/'s own types. That comment is accurate for
   computeAspects called properly with two snapshots, and the new block seventy lines
   later is what corrects it for composeChart -- but a reader who lands on the type
   listing and not on the table will take it at face value. A five-word cross
   reference would close it.
3. GroundTruth's second criterion is the one that matters here and it has not moved:
   five columns are being dropped from a table holding real rows including the Sprint
   14 fixture. The static case is good -- /reading/[id] reads only event_date and
   positions, neither dropped -- but the fixture comparison must be value by value
   against Sprint 14's recorded table, not by eye.
4. Deferred deliberately and now tracked in a sprint file rather than only in my
   notes: saveReading's discarded Supabase error, to Sprint 18.

Cleared to ship at e3f56e7. Standing note for Pipeman: files under docs/sprints/ are
tracked and the tree is dirty with sprint bookkeeping -- do not fold any of it into
the shipped commit, the tree content is what /sprint-ship compares against this
verdict.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 15, commit
e3f56e7d7790c36f40d23c6c1a0c99c8ac533100.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data
API, 2026-08-22 ~23:20Z.

VERDICT: PASS. All three criteria verified. A destructive migration ran against a
table holding real rows and nothing was lost.

CRITERION 1 -- /api/health/db reports the new migration version and the shipped
commit. PASS.
  {"status":"ok","connected":true,
   "migrationVersion":"20260822224620_readings_add_events_and_horoscope_columns",
   "commit":{"sha":"e3f56e7d7790c36f40d23c6c1a0c99c8ac533100",
             "short":"e3f56e7","isLocal":false}}
  - migrationVersion is the newer of this sprint's two migrations, advanced from
    Sprint 10's 20260816181929_readings_positions_not_null. Both new migrations are
    on origin/main: ..._drop_vestigial_place_columns and
    ..._add_events_and_horoscope_columns.
  - commit sha matches Pipeman's ship and origin/main exactly, all 40 characters.

CRITERION 2 -- the Sprint 14 fixture reading still opens and renders identically.
PASS. This is the sprint's actual proof: five columns were dropped from a table
holding real rows, and this is what shows the rows survived it.
  GET /reading/f8d046f7-6432-4961-b996-d65c9f623a8e -> HTTP/2 200.
  Heading "Reading for 1977-03-31" -- matches.
  Compared value by value against the table recorded in Sprint 14's file, not
  eyeballed. All ten bodies match on sign, degree AND retrograde:
    Sun Aries 10.66 No | Moon Leo 22.45 No | Mercury Aries 25.52 No |
    Venus Aries 19.87 Yes | Mars Pisces 8.90 No | Jupiter Taurus 29.39 No |
    Saturn Leo 10.05 Yes | Uranus Scorpio 10.95 Yes |
    Neptune Sagittarius 16.09 Yes | Pluto Libra 12.88 Yes
  Zero mismatches across 30 compared values plus the heading. Byte-identical to
  what the same fixture returned before the migration, at 1dd1e9d.

SCHEMA CHANGE CONFIRMED AGAINST THE LIVE DATABASE, not just the migration files.
  Read the fixture row through the anon get_reading_by_id RPC and inspected the
  returned columns directly. Actual column set now:
    created_at, event_date, events, horoscope, horoscope_generated_at,
    horoscope_model, id, positions
  - All five vestigial columns are GONE: event_time, place_name, latitude,
    longitude, timezone. None present. R1 confirmed in production.
  - All four new columns are PRESENT and NULL on this pre-existing row:
    events, horoscope, horoscope_generated_at, horoscope_model. R2's "nothing
    backfills them; existing readings keep null" confirmed on a real row rather
    than inferred from the migration's text.

CRITERION 3 -- a new reading can still be created and retrieved at its link. PASS.
  This was the criterion most at risk. If any deployed version still wrote the
  dropped columns, saves would have started failing the moment the migration
  landed -- R1 asserts none does, and this is what tests that assertion rather
  than trusting it.
    POST the save action for date=1801-09-09 -> HTTP/2 303,
      location: /reading/d13b041a-71fa-4b45-83cc-fe98009ab034
    GET that link with no cookie jar -> 200, no Set-Cookie, rendered server-side.
  The write path is unaffected by the column drop.

  I CHOSE THE DATE DELIBERATELY. 1801-09-09 is one of the dates I verified against
  NASA JPL Horizons in Sprint 6 (worst error 19.6 arcsec across ten bodies), so
  the new row could be checked for astronomical correctness and not merely for
  existing. All ten bodies in the retrieved reading match those JPL-verified
  values exactly, including Pluto retrograde:
    Sun Virgo 16.28 No | Moon Libra 0.86 No | Mercury Virgo 7.82 No |
    Venus Leo 3.66 No | Mars Libra 0.46 No | Jupiter Leo 22.36 No |
    Saturn Leo 29.94 No | Uranus Libra 1.28 No | Neptune Scorpio 17.11 No |
    Pluto Pisces 4.44 Yes
  Zero mismatches. So the schema revision did not disturb what gets computed or
  what gets stored, only which columns exist.

R8 -- no UI change, four new columns ship empty. Confirmed live.
  The retrieved reading page contains zero references to horoscope, events, or
  generated timestamps. The /chart page's only match for those terms is the site
  title "Retroactive Horoscope" in <title>, which I checked rather than counting
  it as a hit. No new surface leaked out with the schema.

WHAT THIS TEST DID NOT COVER. Criteria 3 through 7 of the requirements --
lib/chart/model.ts, composeChart, its no-recompute rule, isomorphism, and the
date-bound rejection inside the model -- are library-level and have no HTTP
surface this sprint, exactly as R8 intends. Nothing in the running product calls
them yet. They are verified only by QA1's audit and the unit tests, and this PASS
adds nothing to that. The same caveat applied to Sprint 12's aspect engine and
holds for the same reason.

TEST DATA. This test added one production row,
d13b041a-71fa-4b45-83cc-fe98009ab034 (1801-09-09), by exercising the save path
criterion 3 requires. Anon cannot delete. Running count of rows this role has left
in production across the exercise: five. Worth noting that the column drop
silently discarded the place_name values on the older ones, including the
"GroundTruth test - Sea of Tranquility" label from Sprint 4 -- no loss that
matters, but it does mean those rows are now indistinguishable from real readings
by anything except their ids.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks
are curl over HTTPS against production plus direct anon calls to the Supabase Data
API. The pages are server-rendered, so nothing this sprint claims was out of
reach. No JavaScript was executed and no rendering observed.
